entities: plants, algae, and some bacteria convert light energy into chemical energy

triples.head: Photosynthesis
triples.tail: plants, algae, and some bacteria convert light energy into chemical energy
triples.evidence: Photosynthesis is the process by which plants, algae, and some bacteria convert light energy into chemical energy.

triples.head: chloroplast
triples.evidence: In the chloroplast, light-dependent reactions capture energy from sunlight and use it to produce ATP and NADPH.

triples.head: light-dependent reactions
triples.evidence: In the chloroplast, light-dependent reactions capture energy from sunlight and use it to produce ATP and NADPH.

triples.head: Calvin cycle
triples.evidence: The Calvin cycle uses ATP and NADPH to fix carbon dioxide into organic molecules.

triples.head: Calvin cycle

triples.head: Chlorophyll
triples.evidence: Chlorophyll absorbs light most strongly in the blue and red parts of the spectrum and reflects green light, which is why many plants appear green.

triples.head: Oxygen
triples.evidence: Oxygen released during photosynthesis comes from the splitting of water molecules during the light-dependent reactions.
